observations.statement: RGV-010 is an accepted validation rule covering route/open payload fidelity, owner routing, missing context, focused-run and historical coherence, cross-tab coherence, projection trust disclosure, stale tier cleanup, and command-catalog alignment.
RGV-010 names migration validation, plan-index generation and validation, and the plan-governance gates as its validation surfaces.

Phase 2A coverage is required to map every pre-edit span to a fine-grained PlanUnit, preserved source, or explicit disposition, and the migration narrative states that the batch neither refreshed listed governance artifacts nor created executable/build artifacts.

RGV-011 requires an explicit historical_run mode persisted under orchestrator.project_state.{project_id} with focused run, selected node/attempt, snapshot/version, identity, route, trust, action, replay, comparison, restore, back-stack, and warning data; live mutation is blocked until route/action revalidation against current runtime state.

Historical focus acceptance requires a distinct mode, persisted focused_run_ref, visible snapshot/version and live-versus-historical truth, comparison, stale warnings, trust/freshness, and restore/back-stack behavior using the shared route object and project-state key.

RGV-012 requires GoalRun WorkGraph, WorkNode status, SubagentWave, VerificationCycle, repair/retry, blocked/replan-required, receipt, and evidence overlays, while Plan/PlanUnit readiness data is projection-only.

RGV-012 explicitly makes the view a consumer of owner records rather than an authority for WorkNode readiness, capacity, artifact creation, dispatch, or completion; receipt and evidence references must be drillable through owner projections.

RGV-013 projects queued, active, blocked, and completed WorkNodes plus dependencies, model lanes, worktrees, safe points, tests, browser/device sessions, repair loops, Auditor state, configured GitHub state, receipts, and final certification after Executor intake.

RGV-013 limits Run Graph to execution projection and excludes ownership of Plan Compile progress, PlanCompile state, Executor dispatch, and GoalCompletionReceipt certification; several projected categories are conditional on records existing.

RGV-014 says the Orchestrator Plan Compile tab shows source-pack, stage, assignment, coverage, candidate, readiness, audit/repair, blocker, receipt, and handoff information, while declaring no dependencies or unblocked units.
RGV-014 acceptance is framed around source-atom preservation, future audit traceability, and compile-time non-creation, and its named validation surfaces are plan-index and ledger validators.

The FABLE addendum claims the same source-fidelity key is repaired by seven command IDs and five disabled-reason tokens, but the following audit-lineage note still labels that key explicitly deferred and says the source gap has no command IDs or enabled/disabled logic.

RGV-016 consumes UsageRecord projection packets, carries a broad set of identity, lineage, authority, settlement, cost, quota, freshness, health, and counting fields where available, and routes View in Usage primarily from usage_event_ref.

RGV-016 acceptance requires visible source/trust/settlement/freshness and cost/quota unknown-or-hidden truth, preservation of route lineage, child references and dedupe keys across non-happy-path attempts, rejection of weaker primary routing when usage_event_ref exists, and non-ownership of cost authority.

candidate_findings.title: RGV-010 has no behavior-level acceptance oracle
candidate_findings.statement: The rule requires route fidelity, historical/focused-run coherence, cross-tab coherence, stale/degraded disclosure, and live-action trust behavior, but every listed validation surface is a migration, index, or plan-governance command; no behavioral fixture, input case, expected output, or failure oracle is specified in this window.
candidate_findings.impact: A build can satisfy the named governance commands while route behavior, mode coherence, or stale-state disclosure remains incorrect.

candidate_findings.title: Historical live-mutation revalidation is underspecified
candidate_findings.statement: RGV-011 blocks live mutation until an explicit route/action revalidates against current runtime state, but it does not define the revalidation authority, checked fields, freshness/version rule, atomicity boundary, success result, rejection reasons, or behavior when runtime state changes during revalidation.
candidate_findings.impact: Different builders can enable mutations under different stale-state conditions, undermining the stated live-versus-historical safety boundary.

candidate_findings.title: Persisted historical-focus state lacks a concrete schema and transition contract
candidate_findings.statement: The persisted state enumerates many fields but gives no field types, required-versus-optional rules, version/migration behavior, validity constraints, entry/exit transition algorithm, write-failure behavior, or conflict resolution between restored and current selection state.
candidate_findings.impact: Persistence, restore, and back-stack implementations can diverge or revive invalid historical context.

candidate_findings.title: Historical trust and stale-warning semantics are not operational
candidate_findings.statement: The contract requires trust/freshness disclosure and stale-data warnings but does not define freshness inputs, stale thresholds, status values, warning precedence, dismissal rules, or transitions when a historical snapshot is refreshed or disappears.
candidate_findings.impact: The same snapshot may be presented as trustworthy, stale, or actionable by different implementations.

candidate_findings.title: WorkGraph overlay projection has no freshness or degraded-data contract
candidate_findings.statement: RGV-012 defines visible overlay categories and authority boundaries but does not specify projection packet schemas, record versions, freshness markers, missing-owner behavior, partial overlay behavior, or how conflicting owner projections are reconciled.
candidate_findings.impact: The graph can render internally inconsistent readiness, verification, repair, and completion information while still respecting the nominal authority boundary.

candidate_findings.title: Receipt and evidence drilldown is not a complete interaction contract
candidate_findings.statement: The only drilldown obligation says references are drillable through owner projections; route target shape, identity precedence, permission checks, disabled reasons, missing-target response, and error presentation are unspecified.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders can produce incompatible routes or silently fail when evidence is absent, unauthorized, or stale.

candidate_findings.title: Execution-progress reconciliation is left to builders
candidate_findings.statement: RGV-013 lists concurrent runtime and external-source progress categories, including retries, repairs, tests, worktrees, Auditor state, GitHub state, receipts, and certification, but defines no event ordering, idempotency key, retry replacement rule, safe-point precedence, terminal-state reconciliation, or stale/out-of-order update behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: The graph can regress completed nodes, duplicate retry/repair state, or show certification that conflicts with later evidence.

candidate_findings.title: RGV-013 validation defers the behavior review
candidate_findings.statement: The current validation list contains the plan-governance gate and a future Run Graph review, with no present execution-projection fixture or acceptance oracle in the window.
candidate_findings.impact: The post-intake and authority boundaries are not backed by executable evidence at this specification point.

candidate_findings.title: RGV-014 acceptance does not test its user-visible contract
candidate_findings.statement: The canonical requirement lists many Plan Compile tab projections, but the acceptance criteria only require source-lineage preservation, audit traceability, and non-creation, while the validators only check index and ledger structure. No stage model, field semantics, rendering state, route behavior, or visible acceptance case is defined.
candidate_findings.impact: A structurally valid PlanUnit can pass without implementing or consistently presenting any of the listed Plan Compile information.

candidate_findings.title: RGV-014 leaves projection ownership and dependency boundaries ambiguous
candidate_findings.statement: The Run Graph owner document defines behavior for the Orchestrator Plan Compile tab, names Run Graph, Orchestrator, and Final GUI as implementation surfaces, yet declares no dependencies. It does not identify the authoritative producer, state owner, route consumer, or precedence among those surfaces.
candidate_findings.impact: Implementations can duplicate Plan Compile state, attach it to the wrong page, or diverge on which surface owns updates.

candidate_findings.title: The run-graph command repair is not an executable command contract
candidate_findings.statement: The addendum supplies command IDs and a shared list of disabled reasons but does not map reasons to commands, define enabled predicates, payloads, outputs, side effects, selection rules, gesture precedence, cancellation, or error results. The adjacent source summary itself still characterizes enabled/disabled logic as absent.
candidate_findings.impact: Command registries and GUI handlers can implement incompatible pan, zoom, drag, minimap, context-menu, keyboard, and selection behavior while claiming the row repaired.

candidate_findings.title: The same FABLE key has contradictory closure state
candidate_findings.statement: One core line says sfk-e9a741e787bc73207fc9b89a is repaired, while the immediately following audit-lineage section labels that same key explicitly deferred and says repair still requires concrete evidence and no buildability or runtime proof is claimed.
candidate_findings.impact: Auditors and builders cannot determine whether the obligation is closed, intentionally open, or only partially repaired.

candidate_findings.title: Keyboard navigation and multi-selection lack accessibility semantics
candidate_findings.statement: A keyboard_navigate command and set_selection command are named, and the preserved gap explicitly includes keyboard navigation and multi-select, but no focus model, key bindings, traversal order, focus visibility, selection announcement, or assistive-technology semantics are specified.
candidate_findings.impact: The graph can expose nominal keyboard commands without providing a predictable or accessible non-pointer workflow.

candidate_findings.title: UsageRecord projection packet fields have no type or validity contract
candidate_findings.statement: RGV-016 lists identity, parentage, authority, confidence, settlement, cost, quota, freshness, health, and counting fields only as present where available, without types, cardinality, requiredness, null/hidden representation, enum domains, packet version, or invalid-packet behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: Producers and the Run Graph can disagree on identity and status meaning, causing broken routing or misleading totals.

candidate_findings.title: Dedupe and rollup counting semantics are not defined
candidate_findings.statement: The contract requires child usage refs and dedupe_key to avoid double-counting across partial, aborted, retried, escalated, adjusted, and failed attempts, but it does not define dedupe-key scope, parent-child aggregation, adjustment replacement, settlement ordering, or the counting_semantics algorithm.
candidate_findings.impact: Equivalent valid implementations can overcount, undercount, or attribute usage differently during retries and adjustments.

candidate_findings.title: Degraded usage routing has no deterministic fallback algorithm
candidate_findings.statement: The primary usage_event_ref route is explicit and weaker keys are restricted to degraded fallback, but the fallback key order, ambiguity handling, no-match behavior, user disclosure, and recovery path are unspecified.
candidate_findings.impact: Missing usage_event_ref can route to different records or fail differently across graph surfaces.

candidate_findings.title: Usage trust, freshness, hidden, and unknown states lack state semantics
candidate_findings.statement: The UI must show source confidence, settlement, projection freshness, and cost/quota unknown or hidden states, yet the window defines no status enums, derivation authority, freshness thresholds, update transitions, or distinction between unavailable, unauthorized, unknown, and intentionally hidden values.
candidate_findings.impact: Visible totals and trust labels can communicate inconsistent or unsafe interpretations of the same data.

candidate_findings.title: Usage overlay behavioral validation remains future work
candidate_findings.statement: RGV-016 names plan-index and plan-governance checks plus a future Usage overlay fixture suite; no current fixture cases or executable acceptance evidence are identified in the core.
candidate_findings.impact: Primary-route rejection, lineage preservation, and no-double-counting behavior are not presently demonstrated by the listed surfaces.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: RGV-010 explicitly prohibits creation of WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, final node manifests, and production build tasks in this phase.
Migration coverage explicitly requires disposition of every pre-edit Run Graph span and identifies the Phase 2A preservation mapping.
Historical selection is explicitly distinct from the live current run, and live mutation is explicitly gated on revalidation.
Historical stale-data warnings and restore/return-to-live controls are expressly required to remain within the persisted focus-mode model rather than being hidden.
RGV-012 explicitly denies Run Graph authority over WorkNode readiness, capacity, compiler artifact creation, dispatch, and completion.
Failed verification cycles and repair markers are explicitly required to remain visible.
RGV-013 explicitly limits execution progress to post-intake projection and excludes Plan Compile, dispatch, and completion-certification ownership.
The RGV-014 compile explicitly creates no WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, GoalRuns, implementation files, generated governance artifacts, or production build tasks.
The FABLE audit-lineage notes explicitly state that they do not prove repair or buildability and do not create runtime/build artifacts or PNC-019 receipts.
RGV-016 explicitly establishes usage_event_ref as the primary View in Usage identity and rejects tier, timestamp, run-only, or thread-only primary routing when it is available.
RGV-016 explicitly requires preservation of child usage refs and dedupe_key without double-counting the graph rollup across partial and failed-path attempts.

Run Graph is explicitly barred from minting usage authority or recomputing provider costs, and visible usage rows must disclose source, confidence, settlement, freshness, and cost/quota unknown or hidden truth.

unknowns.statement: Whether the dependencies named by RGV-011 define the persisted state schema, revalidation authority, or restore algorithm is unknown because their prose is outside this assigned window.
The exact meaning and authoritative source of current runtime state for historical-action revalidation is not stated in the core.
The behavior when historical state persistence, route restoration, or back-stack restoration fails or conflicts is not stated.
The authoritative version and ordering rules for WorkGraph, verification, repair, receipt, and completion projections are not stated.
What the Run Graph shows when execution records or configured GitHub data are absent, delayed, unauthorized, or contradictory is not stated.
The Plan Compile stage set, transition rules, source-pack immutability mechanism, and route/action behavior are not stated by RGV-014.
The payload, result, enabled predicate, disabled-reason mapping, and interaction precedence for each run-graph command are not stated.
The UsageRecord projection packet schema and the enum domains for source, confidence, settlement, cost, quota, freshness, health, and counting fields are not stated.
The dedupe-key uniqueness domain, parent-child rollup algorithm, adjustment semantics, and degraded route fallback order are not stated.
Accessible names, focus order, keyboard bindings, selection announcements, and non-pointer equivalents for the graph interactions and overlays are not stated.
